app.title: Strassio
docker.set.tooltip: The stone table to take sizes and colours from (e.g. for different suppliers).
docker.preset.tooltip: Saved setting sets and the last 5 settings used to create stones. Pick one — method, stone and parameters are set as in the preset.
docker.preset.save: Save current settings as a preset
docker.preset.name: Preset name, e.g. “Thin stem”
docker.size.tooltip: Stone size from your stone table. Circles will have this diameter.
docker.color.tooltip: Fill color of the circles. The color name goes into each circle's name, e.g. “ss6 Red”.
edit.mode.keepTop.tooltip: Stones lying on top are kept; stones under them that get in the way are removed.
edit.mode.keepBottom.tooltip: The other way round: lower stones stay, stones on top of them are removed.
edit.mode.alongLine.tooltip: Select a cutting line (and stones if needed). Every stone the line crosses is removed — as if the fill were cut.
edit.mode.inside.tooltip: Select a closed shape (and stones if needed). Stones whose centre is inside the shape are removed.
edit.mode.outside.tooltip: Select a closed shape (and stones if needed). Stones whose centre is outside the shape are removed.
edit.mode.shift.tooltip: An overlapping stone moves to a free spot nearby (at most half a diameter). If there is no room, it is removed.
edit.touching.tooltip: Also remove stones lying on the shape border that touch it with their edge.
edit.apply.tooltip: Selected stones, or all stones on the page if no stones are selected. Ctrl+Z undoes everything at once.
edit.duplicates.tooltip: Stones lying exactly on top of each other (e.g. after copying): one of each pile stays — the upper or the locked one.
edit.lock.tooltip: Selected stones will no longer be removed or moved by editing and overlap fixing.
edit.unlock.tooltip: Remove the lock from selected stones.
edit.scope: Works on selected stones; if no stones are selected — on all stones on the page. Locked stones are never touched.
prod.title: Production
prod.bridges.tooltip: Find places with less material between holes than set on the right — the stencil will tear there. Such stones get selected.
prod.bridgeMin.tooltip: How much material must remain between holes, in the current units.
prod.layers.tooltip: Each size on its own layer (“Strassio ss6”, “Strassio ss10”…). Handy for sending to ArtCAM by size.
prod.clean.tooltip: Circles without fill, with hairline outline; Strassio groups are ungrouped. Your own groups stay.
prod.count.tooltip: How many stones of each size and colour are in the selection (nothing selected — on the whole page). The table is copied: paste it into Excel (Ctrl+V).
prod.count.title: Stones to order
prod.count.copied: The table is copied — paste it into Excel or Google Sheets (Ctrl+V).
prod.countDone: Stones: {0}, sizes: {1}, colours: {2}. The table is copied — Ctrl+V in Excel.
vec.offset.tooltip: A new line at the set distance (on the right) from the selected one — outside or inside the shape. The original stays.
vec.distance.tooltip: Offset distance, in the current units.
vec.parallel.tooltip: Several copies of the selected line at a set step — e.g. guides for rows of stones.
vec.count.tooltip: How many lines (on each side, if “both sides”).
vec.step.tooltip: Distance between neighbouring lines, in the current units.
vec.sharp.tooltip: Corners of offset lines — sharp (like the original) or rounded.
vec.split.tooltip: Each selected line is cut into the given number of parts of equal length. The line shape does not change.
vec.join.tooltip: Selected lines with ends closer than the tolerance (on the right) are joined into one; if start and end meet, the line is closed.
vec.tolerance.tooltip: Tolerance: how close the ends must be, in the current units.
vec.close.tooltip: Close lines whose start and end are closer than the tolerance.
vec.gaps.tooltip: Mark with red circles the places where line ends almost meet — the line probably should be whole there.
vec.reverse.tooltip: Reverse the direction of the selected curves — where the row of stones starts.
vec.start.tooltip: Mark the start of each line: the big circle is the start, the small ones show where it goes.
vec.smooth.tooltip: Remove extra nodes and draw a smooth line: a shaky hand-drawn line becomes even — and so does the row of stones.
vec.smoothTolerance.tooltip: How far the line may move from the original, in the current units. More — smoother, but further from the original.
vec.centerline: Centre line from shape or letter
vec.centerline.tooltip: For a thick stroke or a letter — one line down the middle to run a row of stones along (“Along line”).
vec.check.tooltip: Self-intersections and micro-segments are marked; tiny garbage objects and duplicates are selected so you can delete them at once.
vec.hint: Works on selected shapes (groups and stones are skipped). Everything undoes with one Ctrl+Z.
color.recolor.tooltip: The colour chosen above under Stone. Stone size does not change; the name becomes “size new colour”.
color.recolor.hint: Choose the colour above, under Stone.
color.edge.tooltip: Recolours the edge rows of the selected stones — at the outer edge and around big holes — with the colour chosen above under Stone. Gold border and crystal inside in one click. Works with any layout. On the right: how many rows from the edge.
color.edge.rows.tooltip: How many rows from the edge to recolour (1–10).
color.edge.hint: Select the stones of the whole design first: the edge is found from them.
color.artwork.title: Colour from artwork
color.artwork.tooltip: Each stone takes the colour of the artwork shape its centre lies in (where shapes overlap, the top one). The stone colour is the closest one in the table for that stone’s size. Shapes are not changed — delete or hide them afterwards.
color.artwork.hint: Fill the whole silhouette with one method, draw coloured shapes over or under the stones, select everything and click. With only shapes selected, all stones on the page are recoloured.
color.select.hint: Size and colour are the ones chosen above. The selection can then be recoloured, deleted or moved with normal CorelDRAW tools.
docker.create.tooltip: Select a shape or a line and click — the stones appear as one group. Ctrl+Z undoes it all at once.
docker.preview.tooltip: Show here how the stones will be placed, without changing the document. Change parameters and look again.
docker.livePreview.tooltip: The picture recalculates by itself on every change of parameters, stone or method. The shape is the one selected when you pressed Preview.
docker.avoidExisting.tooltip: New stones avoid the ones already in the document (an edge, neighbouring shapes): an overlapping stone moves slightly or is left out. Existing stones are never touched.
docker.colorFromShape: Stone colour from the shape colour
docker.colorFromShape.tooltip: Each shape is laid with the stone closest in colour to its fill. A shape without a solid fill gets the selected stone. You can select the whole artwork at once: upper shapes are laid in full, lower ones go around them.
edit.restoreSize.tooltip: After stretching the design with CorelDRAW tools the circles got the wrong diameter. Each selected stone gets back the diameter of its size from the table; the centre stays put.
edit.fillHoles: Fill holes with the chosen stone
edit.fillHoles.tooltip: Finds empty spots inside the placed stones where the stone chosen above fits, and puts stones there (they stay selected). Selected stones or the whole page.
edit.showUneven.tooltip: Selects stones whose gap on one side of the row is clearly bigger than on the other (more than 0.2 mm difference). Selected stones or the whole page.
edit.evenGaps.tooltip: Nudges stones along the row so the gaps on both sides become equal. The row stays on its line; line ends, corners and locked stones do not move; stones never get closer than the gap in the settings. On the right: how far one stone may move.
edit.evenShift.tooltip: How far one stone may move from its place (default 0.5 mm).
edit.mirror.tooltip: Symmetry: select the stones of half (or a quarter) of the design and press — the plugin builds the other half as a mirror image. Copies have the same size and colour. Stones on the axis are not doubled: a stone right next to the axis moves exactly onto it.
edit.mirror.side.tooltip: Where the axis is: at the edge of the selected stones (through the centres of the outermost stones) or along a straight line selected together with the stones.
edit.updateLive.tooltip: Edited the source line or shape? Select the Strassio stone group and press — the stones are rebuilt along the new line with the same method, stone and parameters.
color.pipette.tooltip: The size and colour of the selected stone are chosen above — then you can create, recolour or select with them.
color.mix.value.tooltip: Evenly and random — share in percent (0 — colour not used). In turn — how many stones of this colour in a row.
color.mix.mode.tooltip: Evenly — exact shares (e.g. 70% crystal / 30% gold), and stones of one colour avoid standing next to each other: even sparkle, no clumps. Random — just shuffled. In turn — by pattern (2 and 1 → C-C-G). Ombre — colours 1 → 2 → 3 flow smoothly into each other (shares do not matter; 0 — colour not used).
color.mix.apply.tooltip: Recolour the selected stones with a mix of colours. Don't like it — Ctrl+Z and again: the layout will differ.
color.mix.hint: Colours come from the size chosen above. Stone names become “size colour”.
color.palette.tooltip: Add all colours from the stone table to the CorelDRAW document palette (with their names), without repeats.
method.l1.tooltip: One row of stones along the selected line or shape outline.
method.l2.tooltip: Several rows along the line or outline: on both sides, outside only or inside only. Overlaps are fixed.
method.l3.tooltip: One row at a set distance from the line — outside or inside the shape.
method.l4.tooltip: The number of rows changes along the line: one row at the ends and all rows in the middle (or from start to end) — a lively stroke instead of an even tube.
method.l5.tooltip: Stone size changes along the line — e.g. ss10 → ss6 → ss5, through all table sizes in between. Stems, leaf tips.
method.l6.tooltip: Sizes follow a repeating pattern, e.g. “ss6, ss6, ss10”.
method.l7.tooltip: Groups of a few stones with gaps between them.
method.l8.tooltip: A big stone at the line ends and/or corners, the rest with the chosen stone.
method.outline.tooltip: Select the whole design (several shapes are fine): a row of stones runs outside around the common silhouette at the set margin.
method.f1.tooltip: Fills a closed shape with a square grid. Holes stay empty.
method.f2.tooltip: Dense staggered fill. Holes stay empty.
method.f3.tooltip: Rows from the edge inwards following the shape; the middle is finished with honeycomb or grid.
method.f4.tooltip: Several rows along the edge following the shape, honeycomb or grid inside.
method.f5.tooltip: Only a few rows along the edge of the shape, empty inside.
method.f6.tooltip: Rows run along the middle of the shape, symmetrically. Good for stems, petals and letters.
method.f7.tooltip: Select two lines: rows flow smoothly from one to the other.
method.f8.tooltip: Select a closed shape and a guide line: rows inside the shape follow the guide's bend.
method.f9.tooltip: Rings or a spiral from the very middle of the shape.
method.f10.tooltip: Stones lie randomly but densely and without overlaps; several sizes can be mixed.
method.f11.tooltip: Big stones in the centre, small towards the edge (or left to right).
method.f12.tooltip: Honeycomb with the main stone, small stones in the gaps left at the edge.
method.f13.tooltip: One row along the middle of a letter or brush stroke. Small stones where the stroke is thin, big ones where it is thick (up to the main stone).
param.gap.tooltip: Distance between neighbouring stones, edge to edge.
param.step.tooltip: How to place stones along the line.
param.exactStep.tooltip: Distance from the centre of one stone to the centre of the next. A gap may remain at the end of the line.
param.exactCount.tooltip: How many stones to place on the whole line. They are spread evenly.
param.startOffset.tooltip: How far to move the first stone from the start of the line.
param.endMargin.tooltip: How much to leave empty at the ends of an open line.
param.reverse.tooltip: Start placing from the other end of the line.
param.cornerAngle.tooltip: If the line turns by this many degrees or more, it is a corner and a stone goes exactly on it. Smaller number — more corners.
param.rowCount.tooltip: Total number of rows, including the row on the line itself.
param.rowGap.tooltip: Distance between neighbouring rows, edge to edge.
param.rowSide.tooltip: Which side of the line to add rows on. For an open line, “outside” and “inside” are just its two sides.
param.stagger.tooltip: Every second row is shifted by half a step — stones sit tighter, like honeycomb.
param.offset.tooltip: From the line to the stone centres.
param.offsetSide.tooltip: Outside or inside the shape. For an open line — one of its two sides.
param.corners.tooltip: How the row goes around a corner. "Mixed" — a stone sits exactly on an ordinary corner, while a very sharp one (a star tip) is rounded automatically: three stones do not fit into a narrow wedge, two go around the tip touching. "Sharp" — always a stone on the corner. "Round" — always rounded.
param.intersections.tooltip: What to do with stones that overlap each other (usually in sharp corners).
param.edgeMargin.tooltip: Distance from the shape edge to the stones, edge to edge.
param.rings.tooltip: How many rows run along the edge of the shape.
param.centerPattern.tooltip: What to fill the middle of the shape with. “Along the shape” — staggered rows run tip to tip, as laid by hand. For smooth shapes — leaf, heart, oval, curved band; letters, digits, stars, circles and shapes with holes keep rings automatically, they are neater there.
param.edgeSize.tooltip: E.g. centre ss10, edges ss6. “Same as main stone” — all rows alike.
param.widthProfile.tooltip: How the line width changes: towards the middle, the end or the start.
param.fromSize.tooltip: Stone size at the start of the line.
param.toSize.tooltip: Stone size at the end of the line. All table sizes in between follow in order.
param.sizePattern.tooltip: Size names from the table separated by commas, e.g.: ss6, ss6, ss10. The pattern repeats along the line.
param.pattern.invalid: The pattern has sizes that are not in the stone table: {0}.
param.pattern.empty: Enter a pattern — size names separated by commas, e.g.: ss6, ss6, ss10.
param.dashCount.tooltip: How many stones in a row in each dash group.
param.skipCount.tooltip: How many stone places to leave empty between groups.
param.accentSize.tooltip: The big stone for ends and corners.
param.accentWhere.tooltip: At the ends of an open line, at sharp corners, or both.
param.autoGrid.tooltip: The add-on tries grid shifts (and a slight rotation) itself and picks the one with the fewest gaps at the edge.
param.centerMode.tooltip: Rings around the centre or one spiral.
param.variant.tooltip: Random layout number: another number — another layout, the same one — the same layout.
param.mixSizes.tooltip: Table sizes separated by commas, e.g.: ss6, ss10. Empty — only the chosen stone.
param.gradientDirection.tooltip: Where the big stones are: in the centre or on the left.
param.fillSize.tooltip: The small stone used for gaps. Should be noticeably smaller than the main one.
param.thinSize.tooltip: Stone for the thin parts of the stroke. The biggest is the main stone; all table sizes in between are used too.
param.invalid: Field “{0}”: enter a number from {1} to {2}.
status.ready: Select a shape, choose a stone and a method, click “Create”.
edit.ready: Select stones (or nothing — then the whole page), choose a mode and press Apply.
color.ready: Choose a colour above and select stones — or select all stones of a size and colour on the page.
status.noStone: The stone table has no size with a color.
status.cannotReadShape: Could not read the shape of the object ({0}). Try “Object → Convert to Curves” (Ctrl+Q) and repeat.
status.noContours: The selected shape has no usable outlines.
status.needClosed: This method needs a closed shape (ellipse, rectangle, closed curve).
status.needTwoCurves: This method needs two selected lines (select both with Shift).
status.needShapeAndGuide: Select a closed shape and an open guide line (both, with Shift).
status.noStones: No stones were placed — is the shape too small?
status.doneConflicts: Done: {0} stones, {1} of them overlap neighbours — they have a red outline. Ctrl+Z to undo.
status.preview: Preview: {0} stones. The document is unchanged — press Create if you like it.
status.previewConflicts: Preview: {0} stones, {1} of them overlap neighbours (red outline). The document is unchanged.
status.design: Done: {0} stones in {1} groups. Ctrl+Z undoes it all at once.
status.designRemoved: Done: {0} stones in {1} groups. {2} left out: they overlapped existing stones or a neighbouring shape. Ctrl+Z undoes it all at once.
status.designConflicts: Done: {0} stones in {1} groups, {2} of them overlap neighbours — they have a red outline. Ctrl+Z undoes it all at once.
status.designPreview: Preview: {0} stones, shapes: {1}. The document is unchanged.
status.designPreviewRemoved: Preview: {0} stones, shapes: {1}. {2} will be left out: they overlap existing stones or a neighbouring shape. The document is unchanged.
status.designPreviewConflicts: Preview: {0} stones, shapes: {1}, {2} of them overlap neighbours (red outline). The document is unchanged.
status.allBlocked: No stones were placed: all {0} overlapped existing stones. Untick "Don't overlap existing stones" if they should go on top.
edit.noStones: There are no stones on the page.
edit.needLine: Select the line to cut along (stones may be selected too).
edit.needShape: Select a closed shape (stones may be selected too).
edit.done: Done: {0} removed, {1} moved. Ctrl+Z to undo.
color.edgeDone: Edge rows ({2}) recoloured: {0} stones → “{1}”. Ctrl+Z to undo.
color.edge.badRows: Number of rows — a whole number from 1 to 10.
edit.sizeRestored: Stone sizes restored: {0}. Unknown size (not in the table): {1}.
edit.noHoles: No holes found where this stone fits.
edit.unevenFound: Uneven spots: {0} (stones selected), biggest gap difference {1}. To fix — «Even out gaps».
edit.gapsEven: Gaps are even: the difference is never more than {0}.
edit.gapsEvened: Gaps evened out, stones moved: {0}. Ctrl+Z to undo.
edit.gapsEvenedSome: Stones moved: {0}. Not fully evened: {1} (selected) — not enough room or shift limit. Ctrl+Z to undo.
edit.mirrored: Mirrored: new stones {0}, moved exactly onto the axis {1}, skipped as too tight at the axis {2}. Ctrl+Z to undo.
edit.mirror.needLine: Select a straight line together with the stones — it will be the axis.
live.none: Select a stone group made by Strassio (or a stone inside it).
live.partly: Groups updated: {0}. Failed: {1} — the source line was deleted or the method no longer exists.
color.pickUnknown: The selected stone has size “{0}”, colour “{1}” — not in the stone table.
color.mix.badNumber: Share fields take whole numbers from 0 to 1000.
color.mix.needTwo: Mixing needs at least two colours with a share above zero.
color.mixed: Stones recoloured: {0}, colours: {1}. Ctrl+Z to undo.
color.paletteAdded: Colours added to the document palette: {0}.
color.artwork.needShapes: Select coloured artwork shapes with a uniform fill (stones may be selected too).
color.artwork.done: Stones recoloured: {0}, stone colours: {1}. Outside all shapes (unchanged): {2}.{3} Ctrl+Z to undo.
color.artwork.replaced: Not in the table, closest used: {0}.
color.artwork.noFill: Shapes without a uniform fill skipped: {0}.
vec.ready: Select lines or shapes and choose a tool.
vec.selectCurves: Select lines or shapes first (not stones).
vec.done: Done: new lines — {0}. Ctrl+Z to undo.
vec.offsetNone: The inward offset is bigger than the shape — no lines were made.
vec.gapsFound: Gaps found: {0} — marked with red circles.
vec.reverseOnlyCurves: Only curves can be reversed — first use Object → Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q).
vec.centerlineNone: Could not build a centre line — a closed shape is needed.
vec.checkOk: All good: no self-intersections, micro-segments, garbage or duplicates.
text.title: Rhinestone lettering
text.hint: Select the lettering: ordinary CorelDRAW text or letters converted to curves. Stone and colour are at the top of the docker; gap and edge margin come from the method parameters.
text.mode.tooltip: How to lay out the letters.
text.mode.middle.hint: For thin and script fonts. Small stones in thin parts, big ones in thick parts (up to the main stone).
text.mode.outline.hint: For large letters: one row along the inside edge of every letter. The stroke must hold two stones.
text.mode.fill.hint: For large bold letters: letters are filled completely with rows along the edge.
text.check.tooltip: Creates nothing: tells you whether the letters are too thin for the stone or too close together, and marks such places with red circles.
text.make.tooltip: Lays out the selected lettering in the chosen way as one operation (Ctrl+Z undoes it all) and checks it as well.
text.note: Red circles are markers; you can delete them. Change letter spacing in CorelDRAW: Shape tool (F10) on the text, drag the arrow on the right.
text.ready: Select the lettering, choose a way and press “Lettering → stones”.
text.select: Select the lettering: text or letters converted to curves.
text.checkOk: Lettering is fine: {0} letters, typical stroke {1}. You can make the stones.
text.done: Done: {0} stones. The lettering is fine.
text.thin: Letters are thin for {0}: typical stroke {1}, needed {2}. Enlarge the lettering {3} times, take a smaller stone or use “One row along the middle”.
text.thinSpots: Thin spots where a stone will not fit: {0} (marked red).
text.tight: Letters are close ({0} apart) — stones of neighbouring letters will merge. Space the letters {1} wider; spots are marked red.
text.overlap: Letters overlap ({0}). Weld them in CorelDRAW (Object, or Arrange in older versions → Shaping → Weld), otherwise the overlaps become holes.
motif.title: Motifs
motif.hint: Save selected stones as a motif (a flower, a leaf, a curl) and lay it out along a line, around a circle or as a frame.
motif.list.tooltip: Saved motifs. The number after the name is how many stones the motif has.
motif.delete.tooltip: Delete the chosen motif from the library. Nothing is deleted from the document.
motif.save.tooltip: Select the motif's stones and click. Sizes and colors are kept. The motif's middle is the middle of the selection, its top is as on the page.
motif.folder.tooltip: Open the motifs folder. Motif files can be copied to another computer.
motif.name: Motif name:
motif.mode.tooltip: How to lay out: along a line, or as a frame with separate corners.
motif.mode.line: Along a line (and around a circle)
motif.mode.line.hint: Select a line, a circle or any shape. On a closed shape the motif's top faces outward, so a circle gives a rosette.
motif.mode.frame.hint: Select a rectangle or any shape with corners. Each corner gets the corner motif, the sides are filled evenly.
motif.second.tooltip: Along a line, the second motif goes every other place. In a frame, it goes into the corners (if none is chosen, the corners get the same motif).
motif.count.tooltip: How many motifs to place. 0 means as many as fit with the given spacing. A frame counts by itself.
motif.spacing.tooltip: Distance between neighbouring motifs, edge to edge.
motif.rotate.tooltip: The motif turns to follow the line. Unchecked, every motif stays upright, as saved.
motif.flip.tooltip: Mirror the motif: its top faces into the shape (for a line, to the other side).
motif.place.tooltip: Lay the chosen motif along the selected line or shape. Stones that would overlap their neighbours are skipped.
motif.around.hint: Select stones and a center shape (a small circle, a cross). The stones repeat around the middle of that shape.
motif.around.make.tooltip: Copies of the selected stones around the center. Size, color and name stay the same.
motif.around.count.tooltip: How many times in total, including the originals (2 to 360).
motif.ready: Motifs: save selected stones as a motif, or lay out a saved one.
motif.selectStones: Select the stones to make a motif from.
motif.noMotif: Save a motif first: select stones and click "Save selection as motif".
motif.selectPath: Select the line or shape to lay the motif along.
motif.placed: Done: {0} motifs, {1} stones. Ctrl+Z to undo.
motif.placedDropped: Done: {0} motifs, {1} stones. Skipped stones: {2}, they overlapped their neighbours; increase the spacing.
motif.around.selectStones: Select stones and a center shape.
motif.around.needCenter: Add a center shape (a small circle or a cross) to the selection; the copies go around its middle.
motif.around.done: Repeated {0} times: {1} new stones, {2} skipped (they overlapped neighbours). Ctrl+Z to undo.
prod.bridgesOk: Bridges are fine: at least {0} everywhere.
prod.cleanDone: Clean circles: {0}, Strassio groups ungrouped: {1}. Ctrl+Z to undo.
docker.stones.tooltip: Stone table: add, change, remove sizes and colours.
stones.title: Stone table
stones.error.setName: One of the sets has an empty name.
stones.sizeName.tooltip: The size name used by your supplier, e.g. ss6 or SS10.
stones.diameter.tooltip: Circle diameter in the template — usually the hole diameter for the stone.
stones.rgb.tooltip: For example #E53935 or 229, 57, 53. Circles in the document are filled with this colour.
stones.addSize: Add size (with colours of the selected one)
stones.copyColors.tooltip: Copy this size's colours to all other sizes: colours with the same name are updated, missing ones are added.
stones.copyColors.done: Colours of size {0} copied to all sizes.
stones.error.noSizes: The table needs at least one size.
stones.error.sizeName: One of the sizes has an empty name.
stones.error.diameter: Size “{0}”: diameter must be a number from {1} to {2} {3}.
stones.error.colorName: Size “{0}”: one of the colours has an empty name.
settings.title: Strassio settings
settings.theme.tooltip: “Like CorelDRAW” — the docker takes the colors of the current CorelDRAW scheme and follows it when you change it in CorelDRAW.
settings.units.tooltip: Units for showing and entering sizes. Stone names (ss6) do not change.
settings.outline.tooltip: How the edge of every circle looks in the document.
settings.outlineWidth.invalid: Outline width must be a number greater than zero.
settings.layout.tooltip: Vertical — sections one under another (docker on the right or left). Horizontal — sections side by side (docker at the bottom or top).
about.title: About
about.noClient: Customer details will appear after the license is checked online (License… → Check now).
settings.license.tooltip: Activation, trial period, computer code, license check.
settings.openFolder.tooltip: Open the folder with settings.json and the stone table stones.json.
transfer.export.tooltip: Save settings and the stone table to one file — to move them to another computer or give them to a colleague.
transfer.import.tooltip: Load settings and the stone table from a file. Your current ones will be replaced.
transfer.imported: Loaded from {0}: settings and stone table are applied.
transfer.error.unreadable: The file could not be read.
transfer.error.notStrassio: This is not a Strassio settings file.
transfer.error.newerVersion: The file was made by a newer Strassio — please update the add-on.
transfer.error.badStones: The stone table in the file has errors — the file was not loaded.
docker.license.none: No license. Click here to activate on the website or start the trial.
docker.license.problem: The license is not active. Click here to open the License window.
docker.update.available: Strassio {0} is available. Click to download.
docker.update.required: This version of Strassio is outdated — please update to {0}. Click to download.
docker.update.title: Strassio update
docker.update.askShort:
New version: {0} (you have {1}).

Download the installer? Close CorelDRAW before installing.
docker.update.error: Could not open the browser. Download the installer here: {0}
docker.update.askAuto:
New version: {0} (you have {1}).

{2}

Update automatically?

Yes — Strassio downloads the installer, checks it and installs it as soon as you close CorelDRAW. Windows will ask for permission once.
No — open the download page in the browser.
docker.update.askAutoShort:
New version: {0} (you have {1}).

Update automatically?

Yes — Strassio downloads the installer, checks it and installs it as soon as you close CorelDRAW. Windows will ask for permission once.
No — open the download page in the browser.
docker.update.downloadingInfo: Strassio {0} is downloading. When it is done, close CorelDRAW — the new version installs by itself.
docker.update.ready: Strassio {0} is downloaded. Close CorelDRAW — the new version installs by itself.
docker.update.readyInfo:
Strassio {0} is downloaded and checked.

Save your work and close CorelDRAW: the installer starts by itself and Windows asks for permission once. Then open CorelDRAW again.
docker.update.failed: The update to {0} was not installed: {1}. Click to try again.
docker.update.reason.cancelled: "No" was clicked in the Windows prompt
docker.update.reason.timeout: CorelDRAW was not closed for a week
settings.checkUpdates.tooltip: On start and once a day the plugin asks the Strassio website whether a new version exists and shows a line in the docker. Nothing is downloaded without your consent.
license.needed: A license is needed — open Settings (the gear at the top of the docker) → License…
license.title: Strassio license
license.copy.tooltip: Copy the computer code — it is pasted on the website, on the Activation page.
license.error.site: Could not open the browser. Open the website manually: {0}/activate
license.error.bad_code: This is not an activation code. Copy it on the website with the Copy code button and paste it whole.
license.activate.tooltip: Paste the activation code (it starts with SA1.) and press Activate.
license.site.opened: The website is open and the computer code is copied. Enter your key there, copy the activation code and paste it below.
license.site.tooltip: Opens the activation page in the browser with the computer code filled in. Enter your key there and get an activation code.
license.trial.tooltip: Free, once per computer. Reinstalling Windows does not reset it.
license.check.tooltip: Check the license with the server. Normally this happens automatically — at every start and once a day.
license.release.tooltip: Remove the license from this computer so the key can be activated on another one. Does not count as a transfer.
license.release.ask: Release this computer? You won't be able to create rhinestones here until you activate the license again on the website.
license.import.tooltip: For a computer without internet: load the license file sent by the author.
license.beta: Beta version: the license check is off for now — everything works without a key.
license.state.wrongComputer: The license is from another computer — get a new activation code on the website
license.state.bad: The license file is damaged — activate the license again on the website
license.state.offline: More than 14 days without contacting the server — connect to the internet and click "Check now"
license.state.clock: The computer's date and time are wrong (set back). Set the correct time and click "Check now" (internet required).
license.done.transferred: Done! The license was transferred to this computer. The old one will stop at its next check.
license.done.released: Computer released — the key can be activated on another one.
license.transfer.ask:
This key is already activated on another computer.

Transfer the license to this computer? The old one will stop at its next check.
The next transfer will be possible in 7 days.
license.error.no_connection: No connection to the server. Check the internet and try again.
license.error.bad_serial: The key is not entered correctly. It looks like STRS-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX.
license.error.bad_license: The server sent an invalid license. Please contact the author.
license.error.bad_file: This is not a Strassio license file.
license.error.wrong_computer: This code or license file was made for another computer. Copy this computer's code and get a new one.
license.error.old_file: This license file is outdated — the license was removed from this computer after it was issued.
license.error.clock: The computer's date and time are set back. Set the correct time.
license.error.not_found: There is no such key. Check for typos.
license.error.blocked: This key is blocked. Please contact the author.
license.error.expired: This key has expired. Contact the author to extend it.
license.error.occupied: The key is already used on another computer. It can be transferred once every 7 days; if you need it sooner, contact the author on Telegram.
license.error.transfer_limit: The license can be transferred once every 7 days. If you need it sooner, contact the author on Telegram.
license.error.not_activated: The license is not activated on this computer. Get an activation code on the website.
license.error.revoked: The license was moved to another computer. To work here, move it back on the website (Activation page).
license.error.bad_request: The server did not understand the request. Update the plugin or contact the author.
